scope: EPL 2025/26 Football-Data versus ESPN kickoff reconciliation

classification_policy.confirmed_schedule_revision: Requires retained evidence that a source published or changed the fixture kickoff, or an independently retained qualified source that corroborates a change.
classification_policy.provider_timestamp_discrepancy: Use only when evidence establishes that the compared provider values represent different timestamp semantics rather than different fixture schedule values.
classification_policy.source_correction: Use only when a later retained source observation explicitly supersedes an earlier source value and preserves correction lineage.
classification_policy.unresolved: Use when source values differ but retained evidence cannot establish a schedule change, timestamp semantic mismatch, or correction chronology. Preserve both observations and do not promote either disposition.

rationale: The February date is in UK winter time, so 19:30 Europe/London normalizes to 19:30 UTC; the ten-minute difference is not a DST conversion artifact.
The retained ESPN observation and Football-Data row agree on teams, date, score, and fixture identity but disagree on kickoff minutes.
Retained evidence has no source publication, update, or revision timestamp that proves which value was first or whether either value was a schedule revision.
No independently retained qualified fixture observation corroborating a change is available in this audit population.
fixtures.eligibility_effect: Keep both source observations and the residual discrepancy visible; do not count it as a timezone artifact or confirmed schedule revision.
